conclusions: The real-converted mass that gaussianReal 0 1 assigns to the singleton set {0} is exactly 0.
mathematical_definitions: The measured set is the singleton {0} in the real numbers.
Measure.real μ s means ENNReal.toReal applied to the extended-nonnegative measure μ(s).
The parameter 1 is nonzero, so the displayed definition of gaussianReal selects its gaussianPDF-density branch rather than the Dirac branch.
translation.proposition_plain_english: The Gaussian measure gaussianReal 0 1 gives zero real-valued mass to the single point 0.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The proposition is closed: it has no binders, hypotheses, or conditional branches.
It concerns only the singleton {0}; it does not assert that every singleton has measure zero or that the measure is atomless.
The equality is about Measure.real, the ENNReal.toReal conversion of the measure value, rather than directly about the ENNReal measure value.

Because ENNReal.toReal sends infinity to zero, the displayed equality alone would also hold if the singleton measure were infinite; finiteness of the Gaussian singleton mass is not encoded as a separate hypothesis.
The positive second parameter 1 prevents gaussianReal from taking its zero-parameter Dirac branch.
The conclusion is exact equality to zero and contains no approximation, inequality, or density value.
ambiguities: The one-level definition of gaussianReal refers to gaussianPDF without expanding it, so the packet does not independently expose the density formula, normalization, or absolute-continuity proof.
The dependency boundary identifies the second gaussianReal parameter only as an NNReal and shows its branch behavior; its further statistical interpretation is not expanded.

No separate finiteness or probability-measure fact is present in the target, so interpreting the Measure.real equality as literal zero ENNReal mass relies on properties of gaussianReal not displayed in the target type.
